claims_and_derivations.claim: When j_p, j_n, R act on mutually independent tensor product factor spaces, they commute, so the scalar triple product chi_geom = j_p . (j_n x R) is already Hermitian without additional symmetrization. Because all angular momenta are axial vectors, chi_geom is strictly P-even and T-odd, invariant under proper rotations SO(3). Under an orthogonal spatial reflection across a plane, axial vectors transform with det(M_axial) = +1, so ordinary spatial reflection does not reverse chi_geom; this handedness is not a parity-odd order parameter. Invariance of chi_geom does not prove the whole oriented state is reflection invariant. T alone also reverses chi_geom; C = T R_y(pi) is the standard convenient body-fixed chiral operation, not the unique possible sign-reversing transformation.
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Three angular momentum operators in disjoint tensor spaces; pure axial vector kinematics.

claims_and_derivations.claim: Standard nuclear chirality transformation C = T R_y(pi) acts on body angular momentum components as J1 -> J1, J2 -> -J2, J3 -> J3. C is anti-unitary; its eigenvalues are phase-dependent and cannot serve as good +/- chiral parity labels. For integer spin I (even fermion number), T^2 = +1 and R_y(pi)^2 = +1; for half-integer spin I (odd fermion number), T^2 = -1 and R_y(pi)^2 = -1; in both cases C^2 = T^2 R_y(pi)^2 = (-1)^(4I) = +1. C^2 = +1 does not protect Kramers degeneracy. In nuclei with both octupole and chiral rotation, the collective potential energy surface does not necessarily form 4 isolated physical wells. Parity projector P^+- defines mutually orthogonal subspaces (P+ P- = 0), but does not guarantee fourfold near-degeneracy (thetwo splittings neednot obey any fixedrelation; accidental equality remainspossible).
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Anti-unitary quantum mechanics; multi-dimensional non-separable potential surfaces.

claims_and_derivations.claim: Delta l = Delta j = 3 is a common and strong coherent driver of octupole collectivity, but not mathematically strictly necessary; E3 allows Delta l = 1, 3 and Delta j <= 3 under parity and triangle selection rules. Near Z approx 56, N approx 88 (e.g. Ba, Ce), driving pairs are proton pi(d_5/2 - h_11/2) and neutron nu(f_7/2 - i_13/2). In actinides near Z approx 88, N approx 134-136 (e.g. 224Ra), driving pairs are proton pi(f_7/2 - i_13/2) and neutron nu(g_9/2 - j_15/2). The Ba pairs must not be applied to Ra.
